why: The criterion holds. I checked all seven expect lines and their proofs. Each one can be checked against the PR head's index.js, README.md and test files. Six use local `node --input-type=module -e` commands or `npm test` plus grep. The README padLeft section uses a "read" proof, and checking it means reading that section for its arguments and return value. Each line has one clear answer: exact return values like '00042', a `## <name>(` heading for every export, and npm test exiting 0. No line needs a release, deploy or published page. "Publishing a release to npm" is listed as a non-goal. One small risk: after shell unescaping, the README-heading regex `'\\\\('` may reach Node as an unescaped `(`. That would throw an "unterminated group" error even on correct code, so the command may need its escaping fixed. Even so, the check itself runs before merge and has no post-merge dependency.
